bug_description.original: Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=4803788135333888 Project: relic Fuzzing Engine: libFuzzer Fuzz Target: cryptofuzz-relic Job Type: libfuzzer_msan_relic Crash Type: Use-of-uninitialized-value Crash State: bn_trim bn_add_imp bn_add Sanitizer: memory (MSAN).
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / exact staged vulnerable workspace / patch.diff
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced MemorySanitizer's use-of-uninitialized-value in `bn_trim` at `src/bn/relic_bn_mem.c:135` on the exact staged workspace HEAD `d9ce2d91842d1a38c7e26e15342b636e5d63609f`. In this snapshot, `bn_mul_karat_imp` splits attacker-controlled operands with `h`, allocates the high-half temporary `a1` with plain `bn_new()`, and therefore gives `a1` only the build's default precision (`RLC_BN_SIZE = 34` digits here) while leaving its digit buffer uninitialized. The function then sets `a1->used = a->used - h` and copies that many digits into `a1` as though the buffer were already large enough. On the reproduced witness, `a1->used` exceeds `a1->alloc`, so the earlier `bn_trim(a1)` guard does nothing. When `bn_mul_karat_imp` later calls `bn_add(a1, a1, a0)`, the saved `bn_add_imp:65` store frame plus the split arithmetic show that `bn_add` keeps `a1` as the longer aliased first operand, so `bn_grow()` reallocates that same `a1` object and leaves the new tail uninitialized. The saved `bn_add1_low:51` frame is the second no-carry remainder loop, so it copies the grown `a1` tail unchanged and returns `carry == 0`; `bn_add_imp` therefore sets `c->used = max`, and the final `bn_trim()` reads that propagated tail digit in `a->dp[a->used - 1] == 0`, matching the saved MSan crash stack. The staged `patch.diff` expresses the same size obligation in a later refactored tree by replacing plain temp allocation with correctly sized `bn_new_size()` calls.

source.description: First exact RELIC-side statement on the crashing path that consumes attacker-controlled operand sizes and materializes the Karatsuba split size used to derive the vulnerable temporary lengths.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the saved libFuzzer input executed by Stage 01. It reaches `cryptofuzz::module::relic::OpBignumCalc`, selects `Mul(A,B)` with `Mul::Run` case 3 (`bn_mul_karat`), and supplies decimal operands that cryptofuzz has already parsed into `bn_t` values before this call. This line is therefore the first exact vulnerable-project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled operand sizes relevant to the bug.

tainted_value_origin.description: Logical length of the high-half temporary derived from attacker-controlled operand size and the split `h`. On the witness, this logical length exceeds the default `bn_new()` allocation for `a1`, forcing the later `bn_grow()` that creates the uninitialized tail.

root_cause.description: The high-half temporary `a1` is allocated at the build's default precision instead of the actual split length `a->used - h`. `bn_init()` does not zero the digit buffer, so any later growth of `a1` exposes unwritten tail digits.
root_cause.note: In this build `BN_PRECI = 1024`, `BN_MAGNI = DOUBLE`, and `ALLOC = DYNAMIC`, so plain `bn_new()` initializes `a1` with `RLC_BN_SIZE = 34` digits. The staged `patch.diff` for the later refactored tree fixes the same obligation by changing this site to `bn_new_size(a1, a->used - h)`.

sink.description: MSan sink. `bn_trim()` reads the top digit of the addition result while trimming it, and on the witness that digit is uninitialized data propagated from the under-sized `a1` temporary.
sink.note: The saved crash stack is `bn_trim:135 -> bn_add_imp:72 -> bn_add -> bn_mul_karat_imp:121`, the MSan store stack points to `bn_add1_low:51` in the no-carry remainder loop, and the heap origin points to `bn_grow:115` inside the same `bn_add(a1, a1, a0)` call.

parser_admitted.description: The staged cryptofuzz input has already been admitted as a BignumCalc request, dispatched as `Mul(A,B)`, and the modifier byte has selected the explicit `bn_mul_karat()` backend that reaches the vulnerable RELIC path.

karatsuba_selected.description: The staged cryptofuzz input selects `Mul(A,B)` and the explicit `bn_mul_karat()` arm, so RELIC executes the vulnerable Karatsuba split/add sequence instead of the generic/basic/comba multiplication paths.

evidence_limitations: The exact reproduced workspace HEAD `d9ce2d91842d1a38c7e26e15342b636e5d63609f` predates the metadata vulnerable commit `bbc7669d7cd5257fd473b7e3b585bb571de28eec`; Stage 02 therefore follows the staged snapshot line map and uses `patch.diff` only as corroboration of the same temporary-sizing fix in a later refactor.

MemorySanitizer directly reports the `bn_grow()` heap origin, the `bn_add1_low():51` store, and the final `bn_trim()` read. It does not separately log the caller-side `bn_cmp_abs(a1, a0)` choice or whether `bn_add1_low()` reached line 51 with zero carry from entry or after earlier iterations, so the closure that `bn_add_imp` operated as `bn_add_imp(c, a1, a0)` and that line 51 copied the grown `a1` tail in the second no-carry remainder loop is source-grounded from RELIC semantics plus the saved line-65 store frame rather than from an extra runtime probe.

coarse_trace.summary: The saved fuzz input reaches the RELIC cryptofuzz module, materializes decimal operands into `bn_t` values, and dispatches the operation as `Mul(A,B)`.
The modifier byte selects `Mul::Run` case 3, so the module calls RELIC's explicit `bn_mul_karat()` backend.
Karatsuba multiplication derives the split size, allocates `a1` at default precision with plain `bn_new()`, then treats `a1` as if it were large enough for the attacker-derived high-half length.

When `bn_mul_karat_imp` executes `bn_add(a1, a1, a0)`, `bn_add` keeps the longer aliased `a1` as the first operand, `bn_grow()` reallocates it, and `bn_add1_low:51`'s no-carry remainder loop propagates the grown uninitialized tail into the addition result.
Trimming the addition result reads `a->dp[a->used - 1]`; that top digit is uninitialized, so MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `bn_trim`.

fine_trace.note: Reachability checkpoint. The staged cryptofuzz input selects the explicit Karatsuba multiplication arm, so control reaches RELIC's `bn_mul_karat_imp()` instead of the generic, basic, or Comba multiply paths.
Source. The first exact RELIC-side statement on the crashing path consumes the attacker-controlled operand lengths and derives the Karatsuba split size `h` that both half-lengths use.

Root cause. `a1` is initialized only at the build's default precision (`RLC_BN_SIZE = 34` digits here), and `bn_init()` does not zero the digit buffer. The allocation is not tied to the actual high-half size needed for this operand split.

The low-half temporary length is fixed to the split size `h`. This establishes the operand length later compared against `a1->used` and later reused inside `bn_add_imp` as `min` when `a1` is the longer addend.

The logical digit count for the high-half temporary is derived from the attacker-controlled operand size and the split `h`. By construction `a1->used` is never smaller than `a0->used = h`, and the later saved `bn_add_imp:65` store proves the witness actually reaches the strict `a1->used > a0->used` case.

fine_trace.code:
for (int i = 0; i < a1->used; i++, t0++, tmpa++)
    *t0 = *tmpa;
fine_trace.note: The copy loop materializes the high half of the attacker-controlled operand into `a1` for `a1->used` digits, so later code treats that many digits as part of `a1`. Because step 3 gave `a1` only the default precision, this logical high-half state extends past the originally allocated prefix.

When `bn_mul_karat_imp` immediately calls `bn_trim(a1)`, this guard is false for the witness because the logical length from step 5 still exceeds the allocation from step 3. That leaves `a1->used` unchanged and carries the oversized logical length into the later addition.

In `bn_add(a1, a1, a0)`, `bn_cmp_abs(a1, a0)` does not take the `RLC_LT` arm. Step 4 gives `a0->used = h`, step 5 makes `a1->used` no smaller than that, and the saved `bn_add_imp:65` store frame proves the unequal-length path ran, so this witness enters `bn_add_imp(c, a1, a0)` with `c == a == a1` and `b == a0`. That makes later `a->dp + min` refer to the aliased `a1` buffer, not `a0`.

Inside `bn_add_imp(c, a1, a0)`, `max = a->used = a1->used`, so `bn_grow()` reallocates the aliased `a1` object. Only the old allocated prefix is preserved; the newly added tail bytes are uninitialized. This is the MSan heap-origin frame.

This store is in `bn_add1_low()`'s second remainder loop `for (; i < size; i++, a++, c++)`, so when line 51 executes the function is copying remainder digits with `carry == 0` and will return 0. Because step 8 made `a` and `c` the same grown `a1` buffer and step 9 left its new tail uninitialized, line 51 copies the remaining `a1` tail digits unchanged from `a->dp + min` back into `c->dp + min`. This is the MSan store frame.

Because step 10 is the no-carry remainder loop, `bn_add1_low()` returns `carry == 0`. `bn_add_imp` therefore skips `c->dp[max] = carry` and records `c->used = max`, so the logical top digit remains the copied tail digit from step 10 rather than an appended initialized carry digit.

Sink. With step 9 having made `alloc >= used` and step 11 setting `a->used = max`, `bn_trim()` reads `a->dp[max - 1]` as the top digit of the addition result. On the witness, that slot is one of the uninitialized grown-tail digits propagated at step 10, which matches the saved MSan crash in `bn_trim` after `bn_add_imp` and `bn_mul_karat_imp:121`.

poc.trigger: The staged `poc` is the saved cryptofuzz/libFuzzer corpus input reproduced by Stage 01. It reaches `cryptofuzz::module::relic::OpBignumCalc`, selects the `Mul(A,B)` operation and `Mul::Run` case 3 (`bn_mul_karat`), and on the witnessed execution makes `bn_add(a1, a1, a0)` take the unequal-length `bn_add_imp(c, a1, a0)` path, grow `a1`, hit `bn_add1_low:51`'s no-carry remainder-copy on the grown `a1` tail, and then let `bn_trim()` read that propagated tail digit as the top result digit.

format.name: cryptofuzz BignumCalc corpus input
format.contract: The saved witness requires a cryptofuzz BignumCalc request that selects `Mul(A,B)` and the explicit `bn_mul_karat()` arm, with operand values such that `a1->used = a->used - (min(a->used, b->used) >> 1)` is both larger than `a0->used` and larger than the default `bn_new()` precision (`RLC_BN_SIZE = 34` digits in this 1024-bit build); `bn_add(a1, a1, a0)` therefore enters `bn_add_imp(c, a1, a0)` and grows `a1`; the subsequent `bn_add1_low()` call reaches line 51's second no-carry remainder-copy loop, so it copies the grown `a1` tail unchanged and returns `carry == 0`; and `bn_add_imp` finishes with `c->used = max`. This states only the saved witness semantics, not a broader proven trigger class.
